one_liner: R package with header-only xoshiro, PCG64 and Threefry engines, Ziggurat distributions and fast sampling; beats base R's RNG.
what_it_does: Replaces R's Mersenne Twister and inversion-based samplers with faster engines: dqRNGkind, dqset.seed, dqrunif, dqrnorm, dqrexp and dqsample.int mirror the base-R names, and register_methods() installs the engine as R's user-supplied RNG so set.seed, runif, rnorm and rt use it. From C++ (Rcpp, LinkingTo: dqrng) you get dqrng::generator<RNG>(seed) wrappers that derive from an abstract random_64bit_generator satisfying UniformRandomBitGenerator, variate<Dist>() and generate<Dist>() helpers, a random_64bit_accessor for the global seeded RNG, and dqsample_int/dqsample_num. Engines: Xoroshiro128++ (the default since 0.4.0), Xoroshiro128**/+, Xoshiro256++/**/+, pcg64, and 20-round Threefry from the sitmo package.
how_it_is_fast: It swaps R's MT19937 and inversion normals for small 64-bit engines and Boost.Random's Ziggurat normal and exponential samplers, with specializations so one 64-bit draw yields both the 53-bit double and the 8-bit Ziggurat layer index (generate_double_8bit_pair). Bounded integers use O'Neill's debiased integer-multiplication method (Lemire's multiply-shift with a rare modulo), and 32-bit requests use both halves of a 64-bit draw. Sampling without replacement picks the algorithm by sampling ratio: a partial Fisher-Yates shuffle above 50%, bitset rejection from 0.1% to 50%, and an open-addressing hash set below that.
when_to_use: R code bottlenecked on rnorm/runif/rexp: README medians are rnorm(1e4) 654.7 us vs dqrnorm 85.9 us.
Unweighted sampling in R, especially without replacement from large ranges: sample.int(1e7, 1e5) 42.8 ms vs dqsample.int 679.1 us; with replacement 7.07 ms vs 296.86 us.
Rcpp, RcppParallel or OpenMP code that needs reproducible independent streams (clone(stream), xoshiro jumps, PCG streams, Threefry counter splitting), as shown in the parallel vignette.
R packages whose C++ code should share one seeded engine with the R session (random_64bit_accessor).
Pure C++ projects only for the bundled standalone engine headers: xoshiro.h (CC0) and pcg_* (Apache-2.0 or MIT).
when_not_to_use: Standalone C++ without R: dqrng_types.h, dqrng_generator.h and dqrng_sample.h include Rcpp, and dqrng_distribution.h pulls in dqrng_generator.h, so outside R use upstream xoshiro/pcg-cpp with Boost.Random or a C++ library such as EigenRand.
Codebases that cannot take AGPL-3 (strong copyleft with a network clause) for dqrng's own code.
Weighted sampling: the C++ dqsample_int ignores prob, and open issue #52 reports R-level dqsample.int with prob about 10x slower than base sample.int for small probability vectors.

When you must reproduce base R's random streams or keep streams stable across dqrng versions: the engines differ, rexp and dqrexp differ even after register_methods(), and the default engine (0.4.0) and seeding (0.3.0) have changed before.

integration.form: R package (CRAN) shipping header-only C++ in inst/include, used via LinkingTo or Rcpp::depends
integration.dependencies: R and Rcpp (the generator, type and sampling headers include Rcpp); BH (Boost.Random) for dqrng_distribution.h; sitmo for Threefry; xoshiro.h and the pcg_* headers are standalone
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (per the vignette); R >= 3.5.0, Rcpp >= 0.12.16, BH >= 1.64.0-1, sitmo >= 2.0.0 (DESCRIPTION)
integration.platforms: wherever R and Rcpp build; PCG64 is disabled on macOS PowerPC and a fallback for compilers without a 128-bit integer was added in 0.4.1; open issue #76 reports 'Cannot install on Windows because of symlink'
integration.thread_safety: The global RNG is not thread-safe and must not be stored or used across threads (dqRNGkind invalidates it); the parallel vignette makes a thread-local copy per thread with clone(stream) under OpenMP, or uses PCG streams with RcppParallel.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the R functions mirror runif/rnorm/rexp/sample.int and register_methods() swaps R's generator in place, but the numbers differ from base R; at C++ level the engines satisfy UniformRandomBitGenerator and work with <random> and Boost distributions

gotchas: The C++ API vignette says operator()(range) returns integers in the closed interval [0, range], but the code (multiply-shift with rejection, returning the high half of x*range) returns [0, range).
Selecting stream k on the Xo(ro)shiro engines runs k jump() or long_jump() calls, so the cost grows linearly with the stream number.

The fast Boost specializations (Ziggurat bucket pair, uniform real) are written for random_64bit_generator and random_64bit_accessor only; passing a derived generator type falls back to Boost's generic paths (open issue #65). The uniform specialization also drops Boost's result < max rejection loop, so rounding can return max.
Every draw through random_64bit_generator is a virtual call; for the tightest loops use the concrete engine type (for example dqrng::xoroshiro128plusplus) directly.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick dqrng when you work in R/Rcpp and want faster drop-in-style replacements for runif/rnorm/sample.int plus parallel streams; zigg is a lighter R/C++ Ziggurat-only alternative, while pure C++ code is better served by EigenRand (vectorized distributions) or the simdrng and VMT19937 SIMD engines.
verified_claims_summary: First-party bench::mark medians in the README, with no CPU, compiler or R version stated: rnorm(1e4) 654.7 us vs dqrnorm 85.9 us (7.6x), sample.int(1e7, 1e5, replace=TRUE) 7.07 ms vs 296.86 us (24x), and without replacement 42.8 ms vs 679.1 us (63x), ratios derived from page data. These time whole R-level functions (a different engine plus Ziggurat vs inversion, plus different sampling algorithms), not a generator against std::mt19937.
status_note: Stale (last commit 2025-06-29, DESCRIPTION version 0.4.1.1, 16 open issues) but on CRAN with CI and coverage; the package is AGPL-3, while the bundled xoshiro.h (CC0) and pcg_* (Apache-2.0 or MIT) headers can be copied on their own terms.
